experiment: Phase-2 scaling spike: frozen-LLM + APIA vs online LoRA
protocol: 20newsgroups A(sci.space vs rec.sport) -> B(comp.graphics vs politics) -> A'(held-out), 600/600/400 samples, single pass, predict-then-update, batch-1
apia_config: frozen last-hidden -> per-dim standardize -> clip -> cubic B-spline (K=10) -> BlockDiagRLS + ContextualMemory(n_slots=3, beta=1, gamma=0.1, eta=5, alpha_ema=0.05, e_gate=1.0, consolidate_every=250). Identical across all model sizes; no learning-rate-like parameter exists.
findings: LoRA's usable lr window shifts with model scale (1e-3 optimal at 124M, divergent at >=355M; 1e-5 starved). Online single-pass deployment cannot grid-search lr.
APIA holds 0.18-0.24 P3-onset across 124M-774M with zero retuning; RLS has no lr.
Update cost is scale-independent for APIA (0.5-1.7 ms) vs LoRA 61->196 ms.
APIA learn state is CPU-resident ~0.25-0.4 MB; LoRA trainable params grow 0.8M->2.4M plus optimizer state.
Tuned LoRA (lr=1e-4, medium) beats APIA on accuracy (0.09 vs 0.18 onset): honest trade-off is fragility-free operation vs best-case accuracy.
